content.title: About
content.content: Hot hibiscus tea is an aromatic beverage made from dried hibiscus (Hibiscus sabdariffa) flowers. It has a vivid red color and a slightly tart, fruity flavor with berry notes. The drink is popular in Africa, the Caribbean, and Asia, where it is served both chilled and steaming hot.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hibiscus flowers have been used in cooking and traditional medicine for over 5,000 years.
In some cultures the drink is called “red tea” because of its deep colour.
It is often served with honey, lemon, or spices such as cinnamon and clove to enhance the taste.
Hibiscus is cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, but dried flowers store well in a dry place.
In several countries hibiscus tea is a traditional remedy for colds and high blood pressure.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Hibiscus contains anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals and support the immune system.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Studies suggest regular consumption of hibiscus tea may contribute to lower blood pressure.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: A warm cup gently stimulates digestive activity and can ease mild stomach cramps.

items.title: Hydration and detox
items.content: The tea has a mild diuretic effect, helping the body eliminate excess fluid and toxins.

items.title: Weight management
items.content: Low in calories yet flavorful, it can help curb cravings for sweets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to hibiscus.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Hibiscus can enhance the effect of certain antihypertensive medications; consult a doctor if you take blood‑pressure drugs.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Large amounts may stimulate uterine activity; pregnant women should limit intake.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The tea’s natural acidity may irritate a sensitive stomach or enamel.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steep 1‑2 teaspoons of dried hibiscus flowers in 250 ml of boiling water for 5‑7 minutes, then strain. Add honey, lemon, ginger, or cinnamon if desired. Drink hot in cold weather or chill for a refreshing summer beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried hibiscus flowers in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly kept, they retain flavor and potency for up to 12 months. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or a change in colour.
